concepts.def: Plates diverge; new crust forms; Mid-Atlantic Ridge, East African Rift.
Plates converge; subduction creates trenches, arcs; Andes, Japan.
Plates slide past; transform faults; San Andreas.

Stationary mantle plume creating volcanic chain as plate moves over.

walkthroughs.body_html: Constructive (divergent) ridges produce mild basaltic eruptions; East Pacific Rise spreads at 15 cm/yr. Destructive subduction zones produce most damaging quakes and explosive andesitic volcanoes (Mount St Helens 1980 VEI 5). Conservative boundaries (San Andreas) produce shallow quakes only.

India-Eurasia collision since ~50 Ma uplifted Himalayas. Range still rising ~5 mm/yr as India moves NE at 5 cm/yr. Mount Everest at 8849 m. No subduction (both continental); thick crust prevents volcanic activity but creates great mountain belt.

Pacific Plate moves NW at 7 cm/yr over a stationary hot spot. Big Island (Hawaii) currently above plume, with active Kilauea and Mauna Loa. Older islands progressively NW; Midway Island formed 27 Ma ago. Emperor Seamounts continue chain northward, marking change in plate motion.
